passage:
Wednesday: In assembly, Neelam's voice cracked in the middle of the pledge, up to a squeak and back down. A few boys sniggered. Neelam's face burned and he stared at his shoes. Gargi, standing next to him, kept looking straight ahead as if nothing had happened.
Thursday: Neelam whispered in class and hid the cracks. At lunch, Gargi said, "Your voice is changing, that's normal. Nobody minds."
Saturday: His father said, "Mine did that. It settles." Neelam read aloud at home, cracks and all, and they laughed together.

qa.q: On which day did Neelam's voice crack in assembly?
qa.a: It cracked on Wednesday.

qa.q: What was Neelam feeling when he stared at his shoes?
qa.a: He was embarrassed, and his face burned after the boys sniggered. The crack was physical, not emotional.

qa.q: How did Gargi help?
qa.a: Gargi ignored the crack in assembly and later said it was normal and nobody minded. Kind peers ignore it.

qa.q: How might Neelam's father seeing it help him?
qa.a: His father said his own voice did that and it settles, which offered reassurance. Neelam could read aloud and laugh.

grounding: A teenager's voice cracks in puberty causing embarrassment, and kind peers and adults reassure that it settles.

passage: Thomas, your grandfather has a story. I'm Noor, and at fourteen I was called to read the morning prayers at the school assembly. Halfway through, my voice cracked. It went up like a whistle, then down like a frog. Boys giggled. My ears burned. But the master, who I'd been afraid of, didn't smile. He said gently after, "Voices do that at your age. It settles in time." A boy called Anwar said, "I didn't even notice," though I knew he did. It settled after a few months. Your voice will do it too, and when it does, let it. Laugh if you like.

qa.q: How old was Noor when he was asked to read the morning prayers?
qa.a: He was fourteen.

qa.q: What was Noor feeling when his voice cracked in assembly?
qa.a: He was embarrassed, since his ears burned and boys giggled. The crack was just physical.

qa.q: What advice does Noor give Thomas?
qa.a: When his voice cracks, let it and laugh if he likes, since it settles in time. Adults and friends can reassure him.

qa.q: How might Anwar's remark have felt for Noor?
qa.a: Noor knew Anwar probably noticed but appreciated that he chose to ignore it. Kindness spared him.

grounding: A teenager's voice cracks in puberty, and an elder tells Thomas that kind peers ignore it and it settles.

passage:
The choir concert was tomorrow, and there was no time to change parts. At the final rehearsal, Ojas opened his mouth for the high note, and his voice cracked, a loud squeak, then a low croak.
A couple of kids snickered. Ojas went red and stopped singing.
Avni, standing next to him, kept her eyes on the music and didn't laugh. She whispered, "Keep going. Nobody cares."
The music teacher, Mrs Pinto, stopped the piano. "Ojas, that's your voice changing. It happens to everyone. It's physical, not nerves. It'll settle with time."
"But the concert's tomorrow!"
"Then sing the lower line tonight. I'll switch you."
Ojas let out a breath. Avni nudged him. "See?"
He sang the lower line, and it came out smooth.

qa.q: What did Mrs Pinto suggest Ojas sing?
qa.a: The lower line.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling when his voice cracked?
qa.a: Ojas felt embarrassed and worried, especially with the concert the next day.

qa.q: What did Avni and Mrs Pinto do that helped?
qa.a: Avni ignored the crack and encouraged him, and Mrs Pinto explained the change was physical and switched his part.

qa.q: How might the kids who snickered see Ojas's voice crack after Mrs Pinto's explanation?
qa.a: They might realise it's a normal body change, not something to laugh at.

grounding: Before a concert, a teenager's voice cracks, a friend ignores it, and a teacher reassures it will settle.

passage:
At a family dinner in their Bengaluru flat, Yogesh was telling a story about his cricket match. Mid-sentence, his voice cracked, jumping high then dropping.
His cousin Rohit burst out laughing. "Did you just squeak?"
Yogesh went silent, face burning.
His sister Indu didn't laugh. She said calmly, "So what happened after the catch?"
Yogesh took a breath and finished his story, voice still wobbly.
Later, Papa found him on the balcony. "Your voice is changing. That's your body growing. Mine did the same at your age."
"Everyone laughed."
"Only Rohit. And his cracked too, two years ago. It settles with time."
Yogesh smiled a little. "Really?"
"Really. Ask Rohit."

qa.q: What was Yogesh telling a story about?
qa.a: His cricket match.

qa.q: What was Yogesh feeling when his cousin laughed?
qa.a: Yogesh felt embarrassed and ashamed, his face burning.

qa.q: What did Indu do that helped?
qa.a: Indu ignored the crack and asked a question to help Yogesh continue his story.

qa.q: How did Papa help Yogesh understand?
qa.a: Papa explained the voice change was physical, part of growing, and that it would settle with time.

grounding: At a family dinner, a teenager's voice cracks, a sister ignores it, and a parent reassures it's physical and temporary.

passage:
"Damini Didi, why does my voice keep doing this?" Omkar's voice cracked on "this," going from high to low.
"Doing what?"
"That! The squeaky thing!"
"Oh, Omkar." Damini put down her book. "It's your voice changing. Your throat is growing, and it takes time to settle."
"But it's so embarrassing. In class, everyone looks at me when it happens."
"Does anyone laugh?"
"Sometimes. Mostly my friends ignore it."
"Good friends. It's not about feelings, it's just your body. It happened to your Bhaiya too, remember?"
Omkar thought about it. "He used to sound like a donkey."
Damini laughed. "Exactly. And now he sings at weddings."
"Okay," Omkar said, and his voice cracked again. This time he laughed.

qa.q: Whose voice used to sound like a donkey, according to Omkar?
qa.a: Omkar's Bhaiya.

qa.q: What was Omkar feeling about his voice cracking?
qa.a: Omkar felt embarrassed, especially when classmates looked at him when it happened.

qa.q: How did Damini reassure Omkar?
qa.a: She explained the cracking is a physical change that settles with time and reminded him of his brother's voice.

qa.q: How do Omkar's friends respond to the cracks?
qa.a: His friends mostly ignore it, which Damini points out is kind.

grounding: A teenager asks an older cousin about his cracking voice, and she reassures him it's physical and will settle.

passage: I'm Ritu, and last year my voice started doing strange things. In the middle of reading the morning pledge, it jumped up high on "India is my country" and then dropped low on "and all Indians". The front rows giggled. I wanted to hide under the stage. After assembly, Parveen Ma'am, our music teacher, stopped me. She said my voice box was growing, that it was my body changing, not me being nervous or silly, and it would settle with time. She told me her own voice had wobbled for a whole year. The next week it cracked again in class, and my friend Nisha didn't even blink; she just kept listening. That helped more than anything. Now my voice is lower and steady, and sometimes I miss the old squeak.

qa.q: Who is Parveen Ma'am?
qa.a: The music teacher.

qa.q: What was Ritu feeling when the front rows giggled?
qa.a: Ritu felt embarrassed and wanted to hide under the stage.

qa.q: What did Parveen Ma'am say that helped?
qa.a: That the crack came from a growing voice box, a body change rather than nerves or silliness, and that it would settle with time.

qa.q: What might Nisha's not blinking have meant for Ritu?
qa.a: Nisha treating the crack as nothing made Ritu feel accepted, which helped more than anything.

grounding: It shows a teenager's voice cracking during puberty causing embarrassment, an adult explaining it is physical and will settle, and a kind peer ignoring it.
